examples.ko: 그 회사는 규모는 작아도 경영이 견실해요.
examples.en: That company is small, but its management is sound.
It is safer to invest in a sound company.

examples.ko: 아버지는 견실하게 모은 돈으로 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: My father opened a shop with money he saved steadily.

examples.ko: 저 친구는 생각이 견실해서 믿고 일을 맡길 수 있어요.
examples.en: That friend thinks in a reliable way, so I can trust him with work.

examples.ko: 이번 분기에도 견실한 성장을 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: It kept up its solid growth this quarter as well.

examples.ko: 견실하지 않은 계획에는 돈을 빌려주기 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to lend money for a plan that is not sound.

explain: 사람의 태도, 회사의 경영, 성장처럼 믿고 맡길 만큼 탄탄할 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '견실한 기업', '견실한 성장'으로 자주 나오고, 반대말은 '부실하다'예요.
explain_en: It describes a person's attitude, a company's management or growth as solid enough to rely on. In the news you often see '견실한 기업' and '견실한 성장', and the opposite is '부실하다'.

en: bitter enemies; at odds (lit. dog and monkey)

examples.en: The presidents of the two companies have been at odds for a long time.
My brother and I have been like cats and dogs since we were kids.

examples.ko: 그 두 사람이 견원지간인 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I did not know those two were sworn enemies.

examples.ko: 견원지간처럼 싸우던 두 팀이 드디어 화해했어요.
examples.en: The two teams that fought like cat and dog finally made up.

examples.ko: 시어머니와 며느리를 견원지간으로 보는 건 편견이에요.
examples.en: Seeing a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law as enemies is a prejudice.

examples.ko: 두 이웃은 견원지간이라서 서로 인사도 안 해요.
examples.en: The two neighbors are bitter enemies, so they don't even greet each other.

explain: 개와 원숭이처럼 만나면 으르렁대는 사이를 빗댄 사자성어예요. 한자는 犬(개 견), 猿(원숭이 원)을 써요. 보통 '두 사람은 견원지간이다'처럼 사이를 말할 때 쓰고, '앙숙'은 서로 미워하는 상대 자체를 가리킬 때도 써요. 반대로 아주 친한 사이는 '단짝'이나 '죽마고우'라고 해요.
explain_en: A four-character idiom comparing two sides to a dog and a monkey that snarl whenever they meet. The characters are 犬 (dog) and 猿 (monkey). It usually describes the relationship, as in '두 사람은 견원지간이다', while '앙숙' can also refer to the hated rival themselves. For very close friends, say '단짝' or '죽마고우'.

examples.en: The professor is sick, so today's class is cancelled.
I saw the cancellation notice and went to the library.

examples.ko: 결강이 생기면 보강 일정을 알려 줘요.
examples.en: When a class is cancelled, they tell us the make-up schedule.
From a student's point of view, a cancelled class is welcome news.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에는 결강이 두 번이나 있었어요.
examples.en: There were two cancelled classes this semester.
The exam range got smaller because of the cancelled class.

explain: 교수님 사정으로 수업이 열리지 않을 때 써요. 학생이 수업에 안 가는 '결석'과 달라요. 빠진 수업을 나중에 채우는 건 '보강'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when a class is not held because of the instructor. It differs from '결석', which is when a student misses class. Making up the missed class later is called '보강'.

examples.en: Judging by the result, that choice was right.
In hindsight, that investment was a success.

examples.ko: 이미 끝난 일을 결과론으로 따지지 마세요.
examples.en: Please do not judge things that are over by their results.

examples.ko: 그건 결과론일 뿐이에요, 그때는 아무도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: That is just hindsight; nobody knew at the time.
The coach answered the hindsight criticism calmly.

examples.ko: 결과가 좋았다고 과정까지 좋았다는 건 결과론이에요.
examples.en: Saying the process was good just because the outcome was good is judging by results.

explain: 과정은 보지 않고 결과만 가지고 판단할 때 쓰는, 조금 비판하는 말투예요. '결과론적으로', '결과론적인 이야기'처럼 자주 쓰고, '지금 와서 하는 말이지만'과 비슷한 상황에 어울려요.
explain_en: It has a mildly critical tone for judging only by the outcome and ignoring the process. It is often used as '결과론적으로' or '결과론적인 이야기', in situations like saying 'it is easy to say now'.

examples.ko: 그분은 결단성이 있어서 회의가 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: He is decisive, so meetings end quickly.
A decisive leader is strong in a crisis.
You are kind, but you lack a bit of decisiveness.

examples.ko: 결단성 있게 행동해야 기회를 잡을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to act decisively to seize the chance.
He relied on his decisiveness alone and rushed the work.

examples.ko: 우유부단한 사람이 결단성을 기르는 방법이 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder how an indecisive person can build decisiveness.

explain: 주로 '결단성이 있다/없다'로 써요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '우유부단하다'예요. '결단력'은 결단을 내리는 힘이고, '결단성'은 단호하게 결단을 내리는 성질이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '결단성이 있다/없다', and the opposite idea is '우유부단하다'. '결단력' is the power to make a decision, while '결단성' is the quality of deciding firmly.

examples.en: This year's farming was ruined by the typhoon.
The car crashed and the front end was wrecked.

examples.ko: 한 번의 실수로 가게 살림이 결딴날 뻔했어요.
examples.en: One mistake almost ruined the shop's finances.

examples.ko: 집안이 결딴나기 전에 빚부터 정리해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to clear your debts before the family is ruined.

examples.ko: 비가 새서 새로 산 가구가 다 결딴나요.
examples.en: The rain leaks in and all the new furniture gets ruined.

examples.ko: 경기가 이렇게 나쁘면 가게가 결딴나지 않을까 걱정이에요.
examples.en: With the economy this bad, I worry the shop will be ruined.

explain: 일, 살림, 물건이 다시 쓰기 어려울 만큼 망가질 때 쓰는 말이에요. '망하다', '엉망이 되다'와 비슷하지만 입말 느낌이 강하고, 일부러 망가뜨리면 '결딴내다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a business, household finances or an object is wrecked beyond easy repair. It is close to '망하다' or '엉망이 되다' but sounds more colloquial, and the form for ruining something on purpose is '결딴내다'.

examples.en: My eyes were red, so I went to the hospital and they said it is conjunctivitis.

examples.ko: 결막염은 다른 사람에게 옮을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Conjunctivitis can spread to other people.
I suffer every spring from allergic conjunctivitis.
If you get conjunctivitis, do not rub your eyes.

examples.ko: 결막염 약을 하루에 세 번 눈에 넣어야 해요.
examples.en: I have to put the conjunctivitis drops in my eyes three times a day.
My eyes itch, maybe because I caught conjunctivitis at the pool.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '눈병'이라고 말하는 경우가 많고, 병원이나 진단에서 '결막염'이라고 해요. '결막염에 걸리다', '알레르기성 결막염'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk people often just say '눈병' (eye disease), while '결막염' is the term used at the hospital and in diagnoses. Common patterns are '결막염에 걸리다' and '알레르기성 결막염'.

examples.ko: 그는 결벽증이 있어서 손을 하루에 수십 번 씻어요.
examples.en: He has a cleanliness obsession, so he washes his hands dozens of times a day.

examples.ko: 결벽증 때문에 남이 쓴 컵은 못 써요.
examples.en: Because of my cleanliness obsession, I cannot use a cup someone else used.
My roommate cleans at an obsessive level.

examples.ko: 저는 결벽증은 아니지만 정리는 꼭 해야 해요.
examples.en: I am not obsessive about cleanliness, but I must tidy up.

examples.ko: 결벽증으로 보일 만큼 깨끗하게 사는 친구예요.
examples.en: My friend lives so cleanly that it looks like an obsession.
My friend says I am a clean freak.

explain: 깔끔한 정도를 넘어서 더러운 것을 지나치게 싫어하는 사람에게 쓰는 말이에요. 가볍게 '나 결벽증인가 봐'라고 농담으로도 하지만, 다른 사람에게 직접 말하면 기분이 상할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes someone who goes beyond tidy and is excessively bothered by dirt. People joke '나 결벽증인가 봐' about themselves, but saying it directly to another person can offend them.

examples.en: In midwinter the river freezes over completely.
Ice fishing starts only after the lake has frozen.
The temperature dropped overnight and the road froze.
The temperature at which water freezes is zero degrees.

examples.ko: 항구가 결빙하면 배가 다닐 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the port freezes over, ships cannot run.
As the weather warms up, the pond that had frozen is melting.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '얼다', '얼어붙다'를 많이 쓰고, '결빙하다'는 딱딱한 글이나 설명에서 나와요. 도로 안내의 '결빙 구간'처럼 명사로 더 자주 보이고, 반대말은 '해빙'이에요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people say '얼다' or '얼어붙다', while '결빙하다' appears in formal writing and explanations. It is seen more often as a noun, as in '결빙 구간' (icy section) on road notices, and the opposite is '해빙'.

examples.en: My parents are fiercely opposed to my marriage.
The residents fiercely opposed building a waste facility.
I am dead set against that plan.

examples.ko: 결사반대 구호를 외치며 시청 앞에 모였어요.
examples.en: They gathered in front of City Hall shouting slogans of fierce opposition.
The union announced it would fiercely oppose the restructuring.
Everyone shouted their strong opposition, but only I agreed.

explain: 목숨을 걸 듯 아주 강하게 반대한다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '결사반대하다'나 '결사반대를 외치다'로 쓰고, 시위 구호에서 많이 들려요. 가볍게 '엄마가 결사반대야'처럼 과장해서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of opposing something as if staking your life on it. It is usually used as '결사반대하다' or '결사반대를 외치다', and is common in protest slogans. People also use it playfully, like '엄마가 결사반대야'.

examples.en: The firefighters brought the fire under control with desperate effort.
He prepared for the exam with a do-or-die resolve.
I ran desperately to save the child.
It was the last game, so the players' faces looked desperate.
My mother's opposition was so fierce that I dropped the plan.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 결사적 수비로 한 골 차 승리를 지켰어요.
examples.en: Our team protected a one-goal win with desperate defense.

explain: '필사적'과 거의 같은 상황에서 쓰고, 반대, 저항, 수비처럼 무언가에 맞서는 말과 잘 어울려요. '결사적 노력'처럼 명사 앞에도 오고 '결사적으로', '결사적인'으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used in almost the same situations as '필사적' and goes well with words about standing against something, like opposition, resistance and defense. It appears before nouns as in '결사적 노력', and also as '결사적으로' or '결사적인'.

examples.en: The city provides lunch to children who go without meals.
I worry that more children go hungry during vacation.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 교회는 결식아동을 위해 도시락을 만들어요.
examples.en: The church in our neighborhood makes lunch boxes for children who miss meals.
The meal support program for underfed children has been expanded.
The donations are used for the breakfasts of children who go without meals.

examples.ko: 결식아동도 눈치 보지 않고 밥을 먹을 수 있어야 해요.
examples.en: Children who miss meals should also be able to eat without feeling awkward.

explain: 뉴스나 복지 정책에서 주로 나오는 공식적인 말이에요. 대화에서는 '밥을 제대로 못 먹는 아이들'처럼 풀어서 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: This is a formal term that mostly appears in the news and welfare policy. In conversation people often put it in plain words, like '밥을 제대로 못 먹는 아이들' (children who cannot eat properly).

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 두 명이나 결원인 상태예요.
examples.en: Our team is two people short.
They posted a job notice to fill the vacancy.
We started this semester with no vacancies.
Many people are on leave, so filling the gaps is urgent.
When a spot opens up, people on the waiting list get contacted.

examples.ko: 결원 때문에 팀원들이 매일 야근을 해요.
examples.en: Because of the staff shortage, the team works overtime every day.

explain: 정해진 인원보다 사람이 모자랄 때 쓰고, 회사, 학교, 동아리에서 나와요. '결원이 생기다/나다', '결원을 채우다/보충하다'로 자주 말하고, 비슷한 말로 '공석'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when there are fewer people than the set number, in companies, schools and clubs. Typical patterns are '결원이 생기다/나다' and '결원을 채우다/보충하다', and '공석' is a similar word.

en: one's untying a knot one has tied

examples.ko: 결자해지라고 네가 시작한 일이니 네가 끝내야 해요.
examples.en: As they say, whoever ties the knot should untie it; you started this, so you should finish it.
I went to apologize in person, feeling I should fix what I caused.

examples.ko: 사고를 낸 사람이 책임지는 게 결자해지예요.
examples.en: Having the person who caused the accident take responsibility is a matter of fixing your own mess.

examples.ko: 결자해지니까 문제를 만든 팀이 직접 고쳐 주세요.
examples.en: Since the one who made the mess should clean it up, please have the team that caused it fix it.

examples.ko: 결자해지 정신으로 갈등을 풀어 보려고 해요.
examples.en: I want to try to resolve the conflict in the spirit of cleaning up my own mess.

examples.ko: 저는 결자해지가 맞다고 생각해서 먼저 연락했어요.
examples.en: I thought I should clear up what I started, so I reached out first.

explain: 문제를 일으킨 사람이 스스로 책임지고 해결해야 한다는 뜻의 사자성어예요. 보통 '결자해지(라고)', '결자해지니까'처럼 말하고, 상대에게 책임을 말할 때도, 스스로 다짐할 때도 써요.
explain_en: This four-character idiom says the person who caused a problem should take responsibility and solve it. It is usually said as '결자해지(라고)' or '결자해지니까', both to tell someone to take responsibility and to resolve yourself to do so.

examples.en: The last goal was the decisive blow for the opponent.

examples.ko: 물가 상승이 서민 생활에 결정타를 날렸어요.
examples.en: Rising prices dealt a decisive blow to ordinary people's lives.
For me, that one remark was the final straw.
This scandal acted as the decisive blow in the election.
It was a pity the game ended without a decisive moment.
The player who went down from the finishing blow could not get up.

explain: 원래 운동 경기에서 승부를 가르는 마지막 한 방을 말하다가, 일의 결과를 정해 버리는 결정적인 계기로 뜻이 넓어졌어요. '결정타를 날리다', '결정타를 맞다'처럼 쓰고 좋은 일에도 나쁜 일에도 써요.
explain_en: It started as the last blow that decides a match in sports and widened to mean the decisive factor that settles an outcome. It is used as '결정타를 날리다' or '결정타를 맞다', for both good and bad things.

en: settle; fix; bring something to a close

examples.ko: 오늘은 이 문제를 끝까지 결판내야 해요.
examples.en: Today we have to settle this problem once and for all.
Let's not fight; let's settle it with rock-paper-scissors.
There is not enough time to settle it through negotiation.

examples.ko: 그 일은 우리가 직접 만나서 결판냈어요.
examples.en: We met in person and settled that matter.
They went to extra time to settle the match.

examples.ko: 이사장은 이번 주 안에 결판낼 생각이에요.
examples.en: The chairman plans to settle it within this week.

explain: 옳고 그름이나 이기고 지는 것을 확실하게 가려서 끝낼 때 써요. '끝내다'보다 승부를 가르는 느낌이 강하고, '결판을 내다'처럼 사이에 '을'을 넣어서도 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when you clearly decide right and wrong or winner and loser and bring things to an end. It has a stronger feeling of deciding the outcome than '끝내다', and you can also say it as '결판을 내다' with '을' in between.

en: have two jobs at the same time; take up a sideline

examples.ko: 직장인이 부업을 겸업하는 경우가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More office workers are doing a side job alongside their main one.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 직원이 겸업하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: At our company, employees are not allowed to hold two jobs.
He works as both a writer and an instructor.

examples.ko: 은행이 보험 판매를 겸업할 수 있게 됐어요.
examples.en: Banks have become able to sell insurance as well.
Because I hold two jobs, I do not even have enough time to sleep.

examples.ko: 가게와 배달을 겸업한 뒤로 수입이 늘었어요.
examples.en: My income went up after I started running the shop and deliveries together.

explain: 본업 말고 덧붙이는 '부업'과 달리, 두 가지 일을 함께 하는 것에 초점이 있어요. 회사 규정이나 뉴스에서는 '겸업 금지', '겸업 허용'처럼 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike '부업', a side job added to your main work, the focus here is on doing two jobs together. In company rules and the news it often appears as '겸업 금지' (dual employment banned) or '겸업 허용' (allowed).
